Both of these are targets of Sinocalycanchinensin G, which in turn targets BMP-2-inducible protein kinase. The scores from the paths indicate a moderate level of confidence in this relationship, with the first path having a slightly higher score (0.6198) compared to the second (0.6048). This suggests that the interaction between Ent-Gloeosteretriol and BMP-2-inducible protein kinase is supported by multiple pathways, though the strength of the evidence is comparable. The shared involvement of Sinocalycanchinensin G as a mediator in both pathways reinforces the possibility of a functional link between Ent-Gloeosteretriol and the target kinase. The evidence is consistent but does not provide direct evidence of the mechanism by which Ent-Gloeosteretriol influences the kinase, leaving room for further investigation into the underlying biological processes.
